items.title: Pseudo-pseudo Meigs Syndrome as the first clinical manifestation of systemic lupus erythematosus after controlled ovarian stimulation for ICSI: a case report.
items.abstract: Pseudo-pseudo Meigs syndrome (PPMS), or Tjalma syndrome, is a rare systemic lupus erythematosus (SLE)-associated phenotype characterized by ascites, pleural effusion, and elevated CA125 without an ovarian neoplasm. After assisted reproductive technology (ART), it may overlap with ovarian hyperstimulation syndrome (OHSS) or mimic gynecologic malignancy. A 25-year-old woman underwent two controlled ovarian stimulation (COS) cycles for intracytoplasmic sperm injection (ICSI) because of severe male-factor infertility. Before ART, she had autoimmune thyroid disease and transient urinary abnormalities, but no known SLE. During the second COS cycle, hypertension and albuminuria emerged. Following oocyte retrieval, she developed massive ascites, bilateral pleural effusions, adnexal abnormalities, and marked CA125 elevation, initially raising suspicion of OHSS and ovarian malignancy. Subsequent nephrotic-range proteinuria, profound hypoalbuminemia, hypocomplementemia, and SLE-associated autoantibodies supported active SLE with substantial renal involvement. Cytologic and microbiologic investigations provided no evidence of malignancy or infection. Following SLE-directed treatment, renal abnormalities and serosal effusions improved. At eight months, the adnexal abnormalities had completely resolved and CA125 had normalized, supporting a PPMS phenotype. Atypical or persistent post-ART effusions, particularly when accompanied by evolving renal or immunologic abnormalities, should prompt consideration of SLE-associated PPMS as an important differential diagnosis beyond OHSS and gynecologic malignancy. Longitudinal evaluation and multidisciplinary assessment may facilitate timely recognition of this rare phenotype and guide appropriate clinical management.

items.title: Short echo time first-echo images of T2* mapping for detecting structural sacroiliac joint lesions in axial spondyloarthritis: a CT-referenced study.
items.abstract: To assess the CT-referenced diagnostic performance of short-echo time (TE) first-echo images derived from a T2* mapping acquisition for detecting sacroiliac joint (SIJ) structural lesions in patients evaluated for axial spondyloarthritis (axSpA), compared with conventional T1-weighted turbo spin-echo (T1-TSE) MRI. In this study, 54 patients underwent SIJ CT and 3T MRI; 52 were included in the final analysis. MRI included T1-TSE and a T2* mapping acquisition; the first-echo magnitude images (TE = 4.36 ms) were used for structural assessment. Two blinded readers scored CT and MRI using the Berlin and SPARCC structural scoring systems. Patient-level sensitivity (SE), specificity (SP), and diagnostic accuracy (DA) were calculated using CT as the reference. Correlation with CT was assessed using Pearson's r, and inter-rater agreement was evaluated (κ for Berlin binary positivity; ICC for continuous sum scores). Forty-three of 52 patients fulfilled ASAS 2009/2011 spondyloarthritis classification criteria. Compared with T1-TSE, short TE-T2* images showed higher diagnostic performance for erosions (SE 88.6% vs 51.4%; SP 70.6% vs 82.4%; DA 82.6% vs 61.7%) and sclerosis (SE 86.2% vs 34.5%; SP 95.7% vs 100%; DA 90.3% vs 62.4%), while both sequences achieved high accuracy for joint space changes (DA 98.2%; T2*: SE/SP 98%/100%; T1: 100%/66.7%). Agreement with CT was stronger for short TE-T2* than for T1-TSE for Berlin erosion and sclerosis sum scores (r=0.913 and 0.921 vs 0.646 and 0.758), with substantial reader agreement for erosion and sclerosis positivity (κ=0.805 and 0.731 vs 0.564 and 0.598). Short TE first echo images from a T2* mapping acquisition provide an accessible, radiation-free, erosion-sensitive approach that demonstrates higher CT-referenced detection of erosions and sclerosis compared with conventional T1-TSE imaging, with strong CT agreement and robust inter-rater reliability.

items.title: Multi-omics profiling identifies a putative Akkermansia -HK3-lactate immunometabolic link associated with JPZS treatment in lupus nephritis.
items.abstract: Lupus nephritis (LN) is associated with aberrant glycolytic reprogramming in renal immune cells, yet its relationship with gut microbial alterations remains poorly defined. Hexokinase 3 (HK3) has emerged as a candidate metabolic node in myeloid activation, while the relationship between gut Akkermansia abundance and renal HK3-associated metabolic changes in LN remains unclear. We used Qihuang Jianpi Zishen decoction (JPZS), an herbal formula used as an adjunct in clinical practice, as an experimental probe to investigate this putative gut-immunometabolic connection through integrated multi-omics. Female MRL/lpr mice ( n = 6 per group) received JPZS (6.305, 12.61, or 25.22 g/kg/day) or vehicle for 8 weeks, with C57BL/6 mice serving as a healthy reference group. Renal function, autoantibodies, histopathology, and glomerular IgG deposition were assessed across treatment groups. Integrated multi-omics profiling-fecal 16S rRNA sequencing, untargeted plasma metabolomics, and renal RNA sequencing-was performed in the matched control, model, and high-dose JPZS groups. Renal lactate and pyruvate were quantified, and HK3 and Ldhal6b mRNA and their corresponding proteins were evaluated by qPCR and western blotting. HK3/F4/80 dual immunofluorescence was additionally performed to examine the spatial localization of HK3 relative to renal macrophages. JPZS reduced proteinuria, serum creatinine, glomerular IgG deposition, and renal histopathological injury in MRL/lpr mice. Gut microbiome profiling showed marked enrichment of Akkermansia and altered community composition, without significant recovery of Chao1 or Shannon diversity, accompanied by reductions in Klebsiella and Enterococcus . Plasma metabolomics revealed remodeling of amino-acid and central carbon metabolism, while renal transcriptomics identified immune-related differences and an exploratory glycolysis/gluconeogenesis enrichment signal. JPZS reduced renal lactate accumulation and the lactate/pyruvate ratio and decreased renal HK3 expression at both the mRNA and protein levels. Dual immunofluorescence showed increased HK3 and F4/80 fluorescence in model kidneys, with overlapping signals evident in merged images; both signals were lower following JPZS-H treatment. Cross-layer correlation analyses linked gut genera, circulating metabolites, and renal gene expression; targeted assays separately characterized renal lactate/pyruvate status. JPZS ameliorated renal injury while inducing coordinated changes in the gut microbiome, circulating metabolome, and renal immunometabolic profile in MRL/lpr mice. Integrated multi-omics and targeted validation identified a putative Akkermansia -HK3-lactate immunometabolic link associated with JPZS treatment. These findings provide a hypothesis-generating framework for gut-kidney immunometabolic crosstalk in LN and warrant future causal validation through microbiota- and HK3-targeted approaches.

items.title: Evodiamine attenuates hyperuricemia-associated gouty arthritis and renal injury through urate-inflammatory axis modulation.
items.abstract: Therapeutic options for hyperuricemia (HUA) and its complications remain inadequate, particularly when gouty arthritis (GA) and hyperuricemic nephropathy (HN) coexist. Agents with combined urate-lowering, anti-inflammatory, and renoprotective effects are therefore needed. Evodiamine (EVO), a major alkaloid from Evodia rutaecarpa , exhibits anti-inflammatory and analgesic activities, but its role in HUA-related disorders has not been fully defined. We examined the effects of Evodia rutaecarpa water extract (ERWE) and EVO in experimental models of HUA, HN, and GA. In the HUA model, ERWE reduced plasma UA levels and increased urinary UA concentration, accompanied by reductions in ALT, AST, and selected inflammatory measurements. Metabolomic profiling indicated that these effects were associated with alterations in pyrimidine metabolism, α-linolenic acid metabolism, and butyrate-related pathways. In the HN model, EVO lowered serum UA and creatinine levels, improved renal pathology, and reduced renal URAT1 and GLUT9 expression. EVO also suppressed NLRP3/caspase-1/IL-1β signaling and reduced the expression of fibrosis-related markers, including α-SMA, COL1A1, and TIMP1. In the GA model, EVO alleviated monosodium urate (MSU)-induced ankle swelling, leukocyte infiltration, and inflammatory mediator production, including IL-1β, TNF-α, and MPO, while inhibiting NLRP3 inflammasome activation. ERWE and the alkaloid EVO showed significant protective effects in experimental HUA-related disorders. EVO, in particular, exerted urate-lowering, renoprotective, and anti-inflammatory activities, possibly through regulation of urate transporters and NLRP3 inflammasome signaling.

items.title: Presumed Paravertebral Inflammatory Pseudotumor in Relapsing Granulomatosis With Polyangiitis: Fluorodeoxyglucose (FDG) Positron Emission Tomography/Computed Tomography (PET/CT) Findings and Complete Metabolic Response to Rituximab-Based Therapy.
items.abstract: We report a case of a 60-year-old woman with biopsy-proven, proteinase-3 (PR3)-antineutrophil cytoplasmic antibody (ANCA)-associated granulomatosis with polyangiitis (GPA), diagnosed six years earlier, who presented with right lower thoracic pain during a disease relapse. The relapse was supported by serological reactivation with a markedly elevated anti-PR3 level, a raised erythrocyte sedimentation rate (ESR) (88 mm/h), and elevated C-reactive protein (CRP) (48 mg/L). Unenhanced computed tomography (CT) showed no pulmonary parenchymal abnormality but revealed soft-tissue infiltration of the anterior and right lateral paravertebral mediastinal fat extending from T4-T5 to T10-T11, without adjacent osseous involvement. Fluorine-18 ( 18 F)-fluorodeoxyglucose (FDG) positron emission tomography/CT (PET/CT) demonstrated intense uptake within the lesion, with a maximum standardized uptake value (SUVmax) of 12.06. Given the differential diagnoses of lymphoma and other granulomatous disease, the lesion was interpreted as a presumed GPA-related paravertebral inflammatory pseudotumor; it was not biopsied. After rituximab and methylprednisolone, the patient achieved complete clinical and biological remission with ANCA seroconversion, and follow-up FDG PET/CT at three months showed complete resolution of the abnormal uptake. Because neither FDG avidity nor treatment response was specific, the presumed diagnosis could not be confirmed histologically in this case.

items.title: Peripartum cardiomyopathy and antiphospholipid syndrome: a rare association revealed by a right ventricular thrombus. A case report.
items.abstract: Peripartum cardiomyopathy (PPCM) is uncommon, and its association with antiphospholipid syndrome (APS) and right ventricular (RV) thrombus is exceptional. We report a 33-year-old woman who, three months after cesarean delivery for severe preeclampsia, developed acute heart failure with severe biventricular dysfunction requiring mechanical ventilation. An RV thrombus was identified; two computed tomographic pulmonary angiograms, one week apart, were negative for pulmonary embolism. Thrombophilia work-up disclosed persistently positive lupus anticoagulant on repeat testing 12 weeks apart, supporting APS. Therapeutic anticoagulation led to complete thrombus resolution after 10 days, and optimized heart failure therapy was followed by hemodynamic improvement and successful extubation. Coronary angiography ruled out ischemic heart disease, and endomyocardial biopsy showed no histologic evidence of myocarditis, supporting PPCM. Myocardial recovery was partial, requiring follow-up within an advanced heart failure program. This case highlights the need to evaluate secondary prothrombotic conditions, particularly APS, and to institute early anticoagulation in PPCM with intracardiac thrombosis. La miocardiopatía periparto (PPCM) es infrecuente y su asociación con el síndrome antifosfolipídico (SAF) y trombo en el ventrículo derecho (VD) es excepcional. Presentamos el caso de una mujer de 33 años quien, tres meses después de una cesárea indicada por preeclampsia severa, presentó insuficiencia cardíaca aguda con disfunción biventricular grave, que requirió ventilación mecánica invasiva. Se identificó un trombo en el VD; para descartar tromboembolismo pulmonar, se realizaron dos angiotomografías pulmonares con un intervalo de una semana, ambas negativas. Se realizó un estudio de trombofilias, diagnosticándose SAF. Se instauró anticoagulación terapéutica, con resolución del trombo a los 10 días. La coronariografía descartó cardiopatía isquémica y la biopsia endomiocárdica no encontró evidencia de miocarditis; el diagnóstico fue PPCM. La recuperación miocárdica fue parcial, requiriendo seguimiento en el programa de falla cardíaca avanzada. Este caso subraya la importancia de la evaluación sistemática de SAF y la pronta anticoagulación en PPCM con trombosis intracardiaca.

items.title: Adult-onset Still's Disease.
items.abstract: Adult-onset Still's disease (AOSD) is a rare auto inflammatory condition characterized by high fever, joint pain, a transient salmon-colored rash, and elevated ferritin levels. Its diagnosis is primarily clinical, relying on the exclusion of infections, malignancies, and other autoimmune disorders. A 23-year-old woman presented with intermittent high fever, polyarthralgia, and a fleeting salmon-pink rash. Laboratory results showed neutrophilic leukocytosis, elevated ESR, CRP, and ferritin (1650 ng/mL), along with mild liver enzyme elevation and negative ANA/RF tests. Extensive investigations for infections and cancer were inconclusive. She met the Yamaguchi criteria for Adult-onset Still's disease. The patient responded well to oral prednisolone and methotrexate. After a relapse at 7 months, treatment was adjusted with increased methotrexate doses, a short course of steroids, and NSAIDs. At a one-year follow-up, she remains symptom-free, with normalized ferritin levels (280 ng/mL) and no signs of macrophage activation syndrome (MAS). Adult-onset Still's disease should be considered in patients with fever of unknown origin accompanied by systemic inflammation. Early recognition and immunosuppressive therapy can lead to remission, even in settings with limited resources.

items.title: Dysregulation of mechanosensing signaling in monocytes of patients with systemic sclerosis is associated with skin inflammation.
items.abstract: Systemic sclerosis (SSc) is a severe autoimmune connective tissue disease characterized by immune dysregulation and progressive fibrosis of the skin and internal organs, resulting in substantial organ dysfunction and increased mortality. Fibrosis is driven in part by infiltration of immune cells, including monocytes that become activated within fibrotic tissue. However, how the mechanical properties of fibrotic skin regulate their function remains poorly understood. Here, we demonstrate that increased stiffness activates human monocytes through mechanosensing. Reanalysis of single cell RNA sequencing datasets revealed that skin infiltrating monocytes exhibit heightened inflammatory signatures as compared to circulating counterparts, with further amplification in SSc. Using collagen-coated hydrogels modeling physiological and fibrotic stiffness, we show that increased stiffness enhances CD86 expression, and broadly upregulates inflammatory transcriptional programs in human monocytes. Mechanistically, stiffness-driven activation was associated with chromatin remodeling and epigenetic reprogramming, identifying the transcription factor Specificity Protein 1 (SP1) as a central regulator. CRISPR-Cas9-mediated disruption or pharmacologic inhibition of SP1 significantly attenuated stiffness- induced inflammatory gene expression, whereas we found no evidence for involvement of the canonical YAP/TAZ-TEAD axis, and pharmacological modulation of PIEZO1 neither reproduced nor blocked the response. Further, monocytes from patients with SSc displayed altered transcriptional trajectories and an exaggerated inflammatory response to high stiffness, accompanied by reduced expression of wound healing and antifibrotic programs. Together, these findings identify SP1-dependent mechanosensing as a previously unrecognized pathway controlling human monocyte activation in the skin and provide mechanistic insight into how tissue stiffness sustains inflammation in SSc.

items.title: Association between systemic lupus erythematosus and clinical periodontal parameters: a systematic review and meta-analysis.
items.abstract: The relationship between systemic lupus erythematosus (SLE) and periodontal disease remains incompletely understood, with conflicting evidence regarding the extent and nature of periodontal involvement in affected individuals. Given the systemic inflammatory burden and immune dysregulation characteristic of SLE, a clearer understanding of its potential impact on periodontal health is clinically relevant. A systematic review and meta-analysis of observational studies was conducted following predefined eligibility criteria, with each study classified according to its actual sampling and measurement structure rather than the design label reported by the original authors. Multiple electronic databases were searched, and studies comparing periodontal parameters between patients with SLE and systemically healthy controls were included. Outcomes assessed comprised periodontitis prevalence, probing depth, clinical attachment level, bleeding on probing, plaque-related indices, and other periodontal and oral health parameters. Random-effects models were used to calculate pooled effect estimates, and heterogeneity was assessed using the I² statistic. Two sets of sensitivity analyses were performed, one a targeted single-study exclusion of the study with the most extreme effect estimate for outcomes with marked heterogeneity, and another removing studies whose values were derived from medians and interquartile ranges. Risk of bias was assessed using the Risk Of Bias In Non-randomized Studies of Exposures (ROBINS-E) tool, and a formal audit for overlapping participant cohorts was undertaken. A total of 20 studies comprising 174,477 participants (3,021 with SLE and 171,456 controls) were included, after excluding two reports for cohort overlap and one conference abstract. Patients with SLE showed a significantly higher prevalence of periodontitis (RR = 1.60; 95% CI: 1.10-2.33; p = 0.01), an estimate that was attenuated but remained significant after removal of the study with the most extreme effect estimate (RR = 1.42; 95% CI: 1.03-1.95) and carried a wide 95% prediction interval (0.40-6.34). No significant differences were found between groups for clinical attachment level, bleeding on probing, probing depth, or plaque index. Gingival index could not be pooled, as only two studies reported it in different age strata, and visible plaque index and salivary pH are reported descriptively rather than as pooled estimates. Salivary pH was consistently lower among patients with SLE in both contributing studies. Neither set of sensitivity analyses, addressing single extreme studies or median-derived values, changed the statistical significance of any outcome, although the magnitude of the periodontitis estimate remained uncertain. Risk of bias, assessed using ROBINS-E, reflected some concerns or high risk in all but one study, driven largely by unadjusted or unreported medication exposure. Certainty of evidence was very low across all seven quantitatively synthesized outcomes. The available evidence suggests a possible association between SLE and a higher prevalence of periodontitis, without corresponding significant differences in most continuous periodontal parameters. These findings should be interpreted with caution given the observational and cross-sectional nature of all included studies, pervasive risk of bias related to unadjusted medication exposure, and very low certainty of evidence throughout. Well-designed prospective studies with standardized periodontal assessment and explicit stratification by disease activity and medication class are needed to clarify the nature and clinical relevance of this relationship.

items.title: Blinatumomab in dermatomyositis and refractory ANCA-associated vasculitis: a 2-patient exploratory study.
items.abstract: This study aims to explore the safety and efficacy of blinatumomab for the treatment of autoimmune diseases. Two patients, 1 with dermatomyositis (DM) and 1 with antineutrophil cytoplasmic antibody (ANCA)-associated vasculitis (AAV), were treated with blinatumomab (CD19 × CD3 bispecific T-cell engager antibody) administered by continuous intravenous infusion for 2 cycles. Evaluations were conducted every 2 weeks until week 12, and then once every 4 weeks during continued follow-up through week 24, as well as on week 56. Immune cell dynamics were assessed by flow cytometry and single-cell RNA sequencing. During the 14-month follow-up, we observed rapid T-cell activation and B-cell depletion in peripheral blood, together with clinical improvement in both patients, without cytokine release syndrome or other serious adverse events. Moreover, 12 weeks after treatment, both T cells and B cells returned towards a state of homeostasis, accompanied by reduced B-cell activation and downregulation of proinflammatory genes in myeloid compartments. Low-dose blinatumomab treatment was followed by sustained clinical improvement over the 14-month follow-up period, together with marked peripheral B-cell depletion and an acceptable safety and tolerability profile. This study provides longitudinal clinical and immunological observations of blinatumomab treatment in anti-Mi-2-positive DM and refractory AAV. These exploratory findings support further evaluation of blinatumomab in autoimmune diseases.

items.title: Imaging Subphenotypes of Thoracic Involvement in IgG4-Related Disease: A Latent Class Analysis.
items.abstract: Thoracic manifestations of IgG4-related disease (IgG4-RD) are heterogeneous. We aimed to identify distinct imaging subphenotypes using latent class analysis (LCA) of chest computed tomography (CT) features and assess their associations with clinical characteristics, radiologic outcomes, and relapse risk. We retrospectively included patients with IgG4-RD and CT-confirmed thoracic involvement. Baseline chest CT findings were independently assessed by two thoracic radiologists. LCA of binary CT features was performed to identify imaging subphenotypes. Clinical and serologic characteristics, extrathoracic involvement, radiologic outcomes, and relapse-free survival were compared across subphenotypes. Cox regression analyses were used to identify factors independently associated with relapse. Among 231 patients, bronchovascular bundle thickening was the most frequent CT finding (56.7%). LCA identified five imaging subphenotypes: bronchovascular bundle-lymph node (BVB-LN, 38.5%), nodular (13.9%), interstitial (13.0%), mediastinal-pleural (18.6%), and mixed (16.0%). These subphenotypes differed in age, respiratory symptoms, extrathoracic involvement, and immunologic profiles. The interstitial subphenotype had the lowest radiologic improvement rate (41.7%) and highest progression rate (37.5%). The mixed (hazard ratio [HR], 3.821; 95% confidence interval [CI], 1.336-10.923; P = 0.012) and BVB-LN (HR, 2.804; 95% CI, 1.062-7.399; P = 0.037) subphenotypes were independently associated with higher relapse risk, whereas combined glucocorticoid and immunosuppressant therapy was associated with lower relapse risk (HR, 0.405; 95% CI, 0.223-0.735; P = 0.003). In this single-center cohort, LCA identified five thoracic imaging subphenotypes of IgG4-RD with specific clinical profiles, radiologic outcomes, and relapse risk. External validation is required before broader generalization or adoption as a standard classification framework.

items.title: Modified immune cell therapy targets kidney-resident tertiary lymphoid structures and ameliorates murine lupus nephritis.
items.abstract: Modified immune cells (MIC), i.e. mononuclear cells challenged with mitomycin C can induce immunotolerance. MIC treatment has been successful in several animal models of autoimmunity and in clinical trials after solid organ transplantation, but the mechanism for reduced inflammation is not fully understood. To investigate the efficacy of MIC therapy in lupus nephritis, splenocytes from syngeneic NZB/W F1 (BWF1) donor mice were incubated with mitomycin C, and then into BWF1 recipients at 25 weeks of age. Animals were followed for another five weeks to assess disease progression by histological, flow cytometric, and serological parameters. An in vitro phagocytosis assay was conducted to determine the clearance of MIC from 25 patients with lupus and from matched healthy individuals by autologous macrophages. In BWF1 mice, MIC therapy reduced the clinical burden of lupus nephritis disease progression with lower protein excretion and lower serum creatinine levels in the standard-dose compared to the control group. High-dose MIC therapy during active diseases showed no additional benefit. More than 86% of animals had dense lymphocytic aggregates close to the kidney pelvis. These tertiary lymphoid structures differed between MIC-treated animals and controls, with a loss of organization, loss of separation of B-cell and T-cell areas and disintegration of germinal centers after MIC treatment. In the peripheral blood, MIC-treated animals had higher numbers of CD19 + CD5 + CD1d high regulatory-like B lymphocytes. Although MIC treatment was beneficial, higher dosing offered no additional clinical benefit in mice. Macrophages from the patients with lupus efficiently cleared MIC in vitro, ruling out defective clearance as a limiting factor. Our clinically applicable cell therapy approach has the potential to control lupus nephritis by specifically dampening deleterious autoimmune responses.

items.title: Engineering long-circulating deferoxamine targeting the innate immunity of neutrophil ferroptosis for systemic lupus erythematosus treatment.
items.abstract: Systemic lupus erythematosus (SLE) is characterized by dysregulation of both innate and adaptive immunity, in which ferroptosis-mediated neutrophil death has been implicated in disease progression. However, the clinical application of ferroptosis inhibitors remains limited by rapid systemic clearance and poor pharmacokinetic profiles. Here, we report a full positron emission tomography (PET)-guided strategy for pharmacokinetic engineering of ferroptosis inhibitors through albumin hitchhiking. By incorporating an albumin-binding motif into deferoxamine (DFO), we developed a series of albumin-hitchhiking conjugates and employed in vivo PET imaging-assisted evaluation to identify a long-circulating molecule, termed LAC NE . Blood pharmacokinetic analysis showed that LAC NE exhibited an estimated terminal blood half-life of 235.94 min, approximately 17-fold longer than that of DFO (13.74 min). Mechanistically, LAC NE was preferentially taken up by activated neutrophils via Fcγ receptor-mediated internalization under inflammatory conditions, resulting in effective suppression of neutrophil ferroptosis. Consequently, LAC NE reduced autoimmune responses, alleviated renal injury, and improved disease manifestations in lupus-prone mice. Collectively, these findings establish a PET-guided albumin-hitchhiking approach for pharmacokinetic optimization and targeted delivery of ferroptosis inhibitors, providing a promising strategy for precision treatment of SLE.

items.title: Emerging Approaches for Phytoconstituent Delivery in the Management of Rheumatoid Arthritis: Bridging Nature and Nanotechnology.
items.abstract: Rheumatoid arthritis (RA) is an autoimmune condition marked by joint inflammation, cartilage destruction, and bone damage. Conventional treatments, including NSAIDs and DMARDs, have shown effectiveness in slowing down disease progression, but prolonged exposure to such medications results in adverse effects and lack of tolerance among patients. In recent times, plant extracts, which are components of traditional medicine practices like Ayurveda and Chinese medicine, have gained interest as potential treatment modalities due to their anti-inflammatory, antioxidant, and immunomodulatory activities. Many phytochemicals have been found to inhibit molecular mechanisms involved in the development of RA, including cytokine signaling, oxidative stress, and immune cell activation. However, their clinical application is hindered by their low aqueous solubility, poor bioavailability, and rapid metabolism. The present review takes a methodical approach for the integration of traditional knowledge with current treatments for RA. It starts with an overview of important plant components with regard to experimentally proven pharmacological modes of action and targets. Thereafter, modern advancements in nano-delivery systems and their use for improving stability, bioavailability, and targeted delivery to inflamed tissues are briefly described. The existing scientific and clinical data on recent developments in this field, along with the latest patents, are also provided. Overall, this review summarizes the journey from traditional phytotherapy to modern approaches in delivery systems, with an indication of research lacunae that have yet to be bridged.

items.title: Catastrophic antiphospholipid syndrome after COVID-19 mRNA vaccination: A case report.
items.abstract: ObjectiveAntiphospholipid syndrome (APS) is a common acquired thromboinflammatory disease and catastrophic APS (CAPS) its most rare and lethal variant. The objective of this report is to describe a case of probable CAPS triggered after vaccination with an mRNA vaccine in the context of the COVID-19 pandemic.MethodsThis is a descriptive case report conducted at a Brazilian university hospital, involving a single 40-year-old patient admitted with dysarthria, gross hematuria, signs of pulmonary embolism, and a large intracavitary cardiac thrombus. He had a history of multiple past venous thrombotic events, but investigations for malignancy had consistently yielded negative results. Approximately 48 hours earlier, he had received the second dose of the Pfizer® mRNA vaccine (Pfizer-BioNTech BNT162b2).After infections and concomitant autoimmune diseases were ruled out, thrombocytopenia and positive serologic testing for APS raised the possibility of CAPS, and treatment was promptly initiated with anticoagulation, corticosteroids, low-dose aspirin, and hydroxychloroquine. Main outcome measures were organ involvement, laboratory abnormalities, imaging findings, and clinical response to treatment.ResultsAfter therapeutic measures were instituted, the patient showed laboratory improvement - restoration of renal function and increased platelet count - as well as clinical improvement, with resolution of neurological deficits. Follow-up testing revealed persistent triple positivity for APS-related serologies.ConclusionsThis emblematic report brings a rare complication of APS in association with immunization using an mRNA COVID-19 vaccine, presenting clinical features that resemble those described in other CAPS cases documented in the CAPS Registry. Additional reports of immune-mediated diseases induced by vaccine platforms have also been described, suggesting pathophysiological mechanisms that remain incompletely understood, particularly molecular mimicry. Immunization against COVID-19 and other pathogens should not, however, be discouraged, as vaccines continue to play a fundamental role in preventing potentially severe infectious diseases. Instead, scientific research should be encouraged in order to better understand which individuals are more predisposed to such a severe complication.

items.title: Multipotent ability of the baseline C-reactive protein-to-serum Albumin Ratio (CAR) to assess current activity and predict subsequent complications of ANCA-associated vasculitis.
items.abstract: To investigate the ability of the baseline C-reactive protein-to-serum Albumin Ratio (CAR) to assess current vasculitis activity and predict subsequent complications in patients with antineutrophil cytoplasmic Antibody-Associated Vasculitis (AAV). Data from the medical records of 319 patients with AAV were retrospectively reviewed. High activity was defined as the highest tertile of the Birmingham Vasculitis Activity Score (BVAS). All-Cause Mortality (ACM), relapse, End-Stage Kidney Disease (ESKD), Cerebrovascular Accident (CVA), and Acute Coronary Syndrome (ACS) were evaluated as subsequent complications. ACM, ESKD, and CVA with significant Areas Under the Curve (AUC) in receiver operating characteristic curve analysis, were investigated. The median age of the study subjects (64.6% females) was 60.0-years. Baseline CAR was independently correlated with current BVAS and yielded the numerically largest AUC for high activity. Patients with baseline CAR ≥ 3.07, ≥ 1.26, and ≥ 14.01 exhibited significantly higher Relative Risks (RR) for ACM (RR = 8.017), ESKD (RR = 3.270), and CVA (RR = 6.660) than those with baseline CAR < 3.07, < 1.26, and < 14.01, respectively. Additionally, patients with baseline CAR ≥ 3.07, ≥ 1.26, and ≥ 14.01 showed reduced cumulative patient, ESKD-free, and CVA-free survival rates compared with those with baseline CAR < 3.07, < 1.26, and < 14.01, respectively. Multivariable Cox proportional analysis revealed that baseline CAR and its complication-related cut-offs were independently associated with subsequent ACM, ESKD, and CVA, except for baseline CAR ≥ 1.26 for ESKD. Baseline CAR demonstrated the multipotent ability to reflect current high activity (the highest tertile of BVAS) and predict subsequent ACM, ESKD, and CVA in patients with AAV.

items.title: Integrated bulk and single-cell transcriptomic analyses prioritize candidate genes associated with lysosomes and ferroptosis in rheumatoid arthritis synovium.
items.abstract: To prioritize candidate genes associated with lysosome-related and ferroptosis-related annotations in rheumatoid arthritis (RA) synovium and characterize their expression across synovial cell populations. Publicly available bulk and single-cell transcriptomic data from patients with RA and osteoarthritis (OA) were integrated with curated lysosome-related genes (LRGs) and ferroptosis-related genes (FRGs). Differentially expressed genes (DEGs) shared by both gene sets were identified. Gene-set expression scoring and high-dimensional weighted gene co-expression network analysis (hdWGCNA) were used to characterize cellular expression patterns and prioritize candidate genes. Candidate-gene expression was assessed in external datasets and by exploratory quantitative real-time PCR (qRT-PCR). Myeloid cells and fibroblast-like synoviocyte (FLS) populations showed relatively high expression scores for the shared gene set. Intersection analysis of the shared DEGs and selected co-expression module genes identified four candidates: VAMP2, HRAS, GRN, and BGN. External datasets supported lower VAMP2 expression in RA than in OA. Exploratory qRT-PCR analysis of synovial samples from four patients with RA and four patients with OA showed a consistent expression difference. Integrated transcriptomic analyses prioritized VAMP2 as a candidate gene associated with lysosome-related and ferroptosis-related annotations in RA synovium. External datasets and exploratory qRT-PCR supported its lower expression in RA. These findings are hypothesis-generating and do not establish a causal role for VAMP2 in lysosomal regulation or ferroptosis. Key Points • Integrated bulk and single-cell transcriptomic analyses prioritized four candidate genes associated with lysosome-related and ferroptosis-related annotations. • Myeloid cells and FLS populations showed relatively high expression scores for the shared gene set. • External datasets and exploratory qRT-PCR supported lower VAMP2 expression in RA, prioritizing it for further functional investigation.

items.title: Mitral valve disease in rheumatic heart disease, systemic lupus erythematosus, antiphospholipid syndrome, and rheumatoid Arthritis.
items.abstract: Mitral valve disease occurs in rheumatic heart disease (RHD) and selected systemic autoimmune rheumatic diseases, but similar lesions may have different underlying mechanisms. This structured narrative review examines epidemiological, mechanistic, imaging, and management evidence, distinguishing established pathways from incompletely validated mechanisms and hypotheses. In RHD, post-streptococcal valvulitis leads to fibrotic remodeling, commissural fusion, and chordal shortening, producing mitral stenosis, regurgitation, or mixed disease. A meta-analysis of 215,552 children and adolescents in endemic settings reported echocardiographically detected RHD in 24 per 1000. In systemic lupus erythematosus (SLE) and antiphospholipid syndrome (APS), typical findings include leaflet thickening, Libman-Sacks vegetations, and regurgitation; embolic complications may occur despite mild valve dysfunction. Among 508 clinically selected patients with SLE undergoing echocardiography, 27.4% had heart valve involvement and 11.2% had mitral involvement. Immunothrombotic mechanisms may contribute to these lesions, but direct validation in human valve tissue remains incomplete. In rheumatoid arthritis (RA), a prospective cohort found an association with incident mitral regurgitation (adjusted hazard ratio 1.54, 95% confidence interval 1.32-1.81), but not mitral stenosis. Myocardial imaging findings do not establish a causal link to regurgitation. These findings support anatomy- and severity-based assessment in RHD, combined valvular and thromboembolic evaluation in SLE/APS, and assessment of conventional regurgitation mechanisms in RA. The framework informs clinical interpretation within existing guidelines, while proposed disease-specific mechanisms require further validation.

items.title: Milwaukee shoulder syndrome: a neglected and underrecognized basic calcium phosphate crystal arthropathy.
items.abstract: Milwaukee Shoulder Syndrome (MSS) is a rare but extremely aggressive form of destructive arthropathy, primarily affecting elderly women. Despite its distinct clinical profile, it remains an under-recognized and frequently misdiagnosed entity. This review synthesizes current knowledge on pathogenesis, clinical presentation, and diagnostic nuances of MSS to improve clinical recognition. The condition is defined by the intra-articular deposition of basic calcium phosphate (BCP) crystals, such as hydroxyapatite. These crystals trigger the release of proteolytic enzymes, leading to massive rotator cuff tears, superior migration of the humeral head, and rapid joint destruction. A hallmark of MSS is the "inflammatory paradox": a striking dissociation between severe structural damage and a non-inflammatory or minimally inflammatory synovial fluid profile (typically < 2,000 cells/mm3), which often is hemorrhagic. Diagnosis is challenged by the nanocrystalline nature of BCP crystals, which are non-birefringent and invisible under standard polarized light microscopy, requiring specialized staining (Alizarin Red) or advanced analytics for confirmation. Multimodal imaging is essential, with plain radiography showing advanced degeneration and MRI or CT delineating the extent of soft tissue and bony destruction. Treatment is currently limited to supportive measures, including recurrent joint aspiration, analgesia, and physical therapy. In advanced cases, reverse total shoulder arthroplasty remains the primary surgical intervention for functional restoration. As the aging population grows, increasing clinician awareness of MSS-particularly its unique synovial fluid characteristics-is vital for reducing diagnostic delay and optimizing patient care.

items.title: Foot and ankle involvement is common across the spondyloarthritis spectrum with distinct anatomical and clinical patterns: a post hoc cross-sectional analysis of the ASAS-PerSpA study.
items.abstract: Foot and ankle involvement is a common but frequently overlooked manifestation of spondyloarthritis (SpA). This study aimed to evaluate the frequency, anatomical patterns, and factors associated with foot and ankle involvement in a SpA cohort. This post hoc analysis included 489 patients from the Turkish cohort of the ASAS-PerSpA study. Foot and ankle involvement was defined as the presence of arthritis, enthesitis, and/or dactylitis. Anatomical distribution of each manifestation was analyzed, and demographic and clinical characteristics were compared between patients with and without involvement. Multivariable logistic regression was performed to identify factors independently associated with foot and ankle involvement. Foot and ankle involvement was identified in 229 of 489 patients (46.8%). Enthesitis was the predominant manifestation (184/489, 37.6%), followed by arthritis (122/489, 24.9%) and dactylitis (27/489, 5.5%). Overall involvement was most frequent in peripheral SpA (28/35, 80.0%) and psoriatic arthritis (PsA) (52/73, 71.2%). The ankle represented the predominant site of arthritis, whereas the plantar fascia and Achilles tendon were the most frequently involved entheses. Isolated enthesitis was the most common presentation, although arthritis and enthesitis frequently coexisted. Patients with foot and ankle involvement had significantly higher disease activity, greater peripheral structural damage, and worse health status than those without involvement (p < 0.05). In multivariable analysis, psoriasis (OR 2.04, 95% CI 1.11-3.76) and higher ASAS Health Index scores (OR 1.11 per point, 95% CI 1.04-1.18) were independently associated with foot and ankle involvement, whereas axial involvement showed an inverse association (OR 0.48, 95% CI 0.24-0.97). Foot and ankle involvement affects nearly half of patients with SpA and is particularly frequent in peripheral SpA and PsA. Enthesitis is the most common manifestation, and poorer overall health status is independently associated with foot and ankle involvement. These findings highlight the clinical relevance of foot and ankle manifestations across the SpA spectrum.

items.title: Incident generalized anxiety and common mental disorders in rheumatoid arthritis: a 12-year case-cohort analysis from ELSA-Brasil.
items.abstract: Rheumatoid arthritis (RA) is associated with mental health disorders, but longitudinal evidence remains limited. To examine the association of RA with depressive episode, generalized anxiety disorder (GAD), and common mental disorders (CMD) in the Brazilian Longitudinal Study of Adult Health (ELSA-Brasil). This case-cohort analysis included 1,795 participants: 252 in the RA case group and 1,543 in a randomly selected reference sample. For each incident outcome, participants with the condition at baseline or without follow-up information were excluded. Outcomes were assessed over 12 years of follow-up. Logistic regression estimated odds ratios (ORs) and 95% confidence intervals (CIs), adjusted for sociodemographic and clinical covariates. At baseline, depressive episode was present in 19 (7.5%) participants in the RA group and 60 (3.9%) in the reference sample, GAD in 45 (18.1%) and 186 (12.2%), and CMD in 92 (36.5%) and 411 (26.6%), respectively. Fully adjusted ORs for the association of RA with depressive episode, GAD, and CMD were 1.52 (95% CI 0.85-2.74), 1.30 (0.89-1.90), and 1.41 (1.04-1.90), respectively. During follow-up, depressive episode occurred in 24 (14.4%) participants in the RA group and 94 (9.4%) in the reference sample, GAD in 37 (25.2%) and 120 (13.3%), and CMD in 43 (36.4%) and 164 (20.9%), respectively. Corresponding fully adjusted ORs were 1.41 (0.84-2.36), 2.04 (1.30-3.18), and 2.06 (1.33-3.18), respectively. RA was associated with baseline CMD and incident GAD and CMD, but not with baseline depressive episode, baseline GAD, or incident depressive episode after adjustment.

items.title: Brepocitinib (Lisraya ® ), a first orally administered small molecule dual TYK2/JAK1 inhibitor approved for dermatomyositis in adults.
items.abstract: Dermatomyositis is a rare systemic autoimmune disease characterized by chronic inflammation, progressive muscle weakness, and prominent cutaneous manifestations, with limited approved treatment options. Brepocitinib (Lisraya ® ), an orally administered dual tyrosine kinase 2 (TYK2) and Janus kinase 1 (JAK1) inhibitor, received the U.S. Food and Drug Administration approval on August 27, 2026, for the treatment of dermatomyositis in adults. Unlike broader JAK inhibitors, brepocitinib exhibits preferential activity against JAK1 and TYK2 over JAK2 and JAK3, providing a differentiated kinase-selectivity profile. In the phase 3 VALOR trial, once-daily brepocitinib 30 mg significantly improved the Total Improvement Score and multiple measures of dermatomyositis disease activity compared with placebo. Its approval highlights the successful application of kinase-directed medicinal chemistry to a rare autoimmune disease and provides a new oral therapeutic option for adults with dermatomyositis. items.title: Patient selection for advanced B-cell-targeted therapy trials in systemic lupus erythematosus.
items.abstract: BackgroundA proportion of patients with systemic lupus erythematosus (SLE) remain refractory to standard therapies. Advanced B-cell-targeted therapies (ABT), including chimeric antigen receptor T-cell therapy, T-cell-engaging approaches, and anti-CD19 monoclonal antibodies, are emerging for selected patients in clinical trials.MethodsWe conducted a single-centre observational study of patients with SLE treated with biologic therapies at a tertiary lupus service between January 2024 and December 2025, during active recruitment to ABT clinical trials. We assessed clinical factors associated with referral for multidisciplinary team (MDT) discussion regarding ABT and explored documented reasons for non-participation. We compared patients discussed at ABT-MDT with those not referred within the same cohort.ResultsAmong 101 patients treated with biologics, 21 (20.8%) were discussed at ABT-MDT. Patients referred for ABT-MDT had higher rates of lupus nephritis (90.5% vs 46.2%, p < 0.001), higher SLEDAI-2K scores (16.0 vs 2.0, p < 0.001), higher daily prednisolone doses (15.0 vs 1.0 mg, p < 0.001), and greater exposure to prior immunosuppressive therapies. In multivariable analysis, higher SLEDAI-2K (OR 1.92 per 4-point increase, 95% CI 1.10-4.27) and prednisolone dose (OR 3.44 per 5-mg increase, 95% CI 1.23-14.50) were independently associated with ABT-MDT referral. Of those discussed, 7 patients proceeded to ABT. Reasons for non-participation included patient preference, perceived infection risk, clinical improvement, and protocol-related constraints.ConclusionIn a tertiary SLE cohort, referral for advanced B-cell-targeted therapies was associated with markers of high disease activity and renal involvement. However, multiple clinical and patient-related factors limited trial participation. These findings highlight important considerations in referral and trial participation for advanced B-cell-targeted therapies.

items.title: Development of quality indicators for systemic sclerosis patients.
items.abstract: To develop quality indicators for evaluating and improving care for patients with systemic sclerosis. We developed quality indicators using a modified RAND/University of California Los Angeles Appropriateness Method. A systematic literature review identified candidate items from previous systemic sclerosis quality indicator studies and clinical practice guidelines. A multidisciplinary expert panel of 10 physicians specializing in rheumatology, dermatology, pediatrics and cardiology completed two anonymous rating rounds, with item revision after a web-based panel meeting. One physiotherapist and one patient with systemic sclerosis participated as non-voting observers. Items with a median appropriateness score of 7 or higher and strict agreement were retained. The review identified 86 candidate items from three quality indicator studies and 23 clinical practice guidelines. After first-round rating and discussion, 78 revised items underwent second-round evaluation. Thirty-three indicators met the prespecified selection criteria. The final set covered general management, lung, gastrointestinal, kidney, heart, pulmonary hypertension, vascular, muscle, rehabilitation, and pediatric domains. We developed a 33-item quality indicator set for systemic sclerosis through a structured consensus process. The indicators may support quality assessment and improvement in Japanese clinical practice.

items.title: Dysphagia as the Initial Manifestation of Anti-HMGCR Antibody-Positive Immune-Mediated Necrotizing Myopathy Complicated by Pulmonary Embolism.
items.abstract: Anti-3-hydroxy-3-methylglutaryl-coenzyme A reductase (anti-HMGCR) antibody-positive immune-mediated necrotizing myopathy (IMNM) is a rare autoimmune myopathy characterized by progressive proximal muscle weakness and markedly elevated creatine kinase levels. Although commonly associated with prior statin exposure, statin-naïve cases and atypical presentations are well described. Patients with idiopathic inflammatory myopathies are also at increased risk for venous thromboembolism (VTE), though data specific to IMNM remain limited. An 83-year-old man with brief, remote statin exposure presented with progressive proximal muscle weakness and a three-year history of oropharyngeal dysphagia preceding limb involvement. Laboratory evaluation revealed markedly elevated creatine kinase and transaminases. Anti-HMGCR antibodies were positive, and muscle biopsy confirmed necrotizing myopathy. During evaluation for occult malignancy, bilateral pulmonary emboli were incidentally identified. The patient required high-dose corticosteroids, mycophenolate mofetil, and intravenous immunoglobulin for refractory disease. With aggressive immunosuppressive therapy and rehabilitation, he demonstrated substantial clinical recovery at 6 months. This case highlights oropharyngeal dysphagia as an early and, for a prolonged period, isolated manifestation of anti-HMGCR antibody-positive IMNM; here, it preceded the onset of limb weakness by approximately 3 years. It underscores the importance of comprehensive diagnostic evaluation in patients with unexplained oropharyngeal dysfunction, in whom an inflammatory myopathy may otherwise be overlooked for years. Clinicians should maintain awareness of thrombotic risk in inflammatory myopathies, particularly during active disease. Early recognition and prompt immunosuppressive therapy remain critical to optimize outcomes and prevent irreversible muscle damage.

items.title: Ethnic Differences in Clinical Manifestations of Behçet's Disease: A Retrospective Cohort Study of Turkic and Non-Turkic Patients.
items.abstract: Behçet's disease (BD) is a multisystem inflammatory vasculitis with clinical heterogeneity that may vary across ethnic groups within the same country. This study aimed to evaluate the influence of ethnicity on the clinical manifestations, immunogenic laboratory findings and disease course of BD by comparing Turkic and non-Turkic patients in a large Iranian referral cohort. In this retrospective cohort study, 2697 patients with BD followed at the BD clinic of Shariati Hospital in Tehran, Iran, from 2007 to 2019 were included. Patients were stratified by ethnicity into Turkic (N = 1037; 38.5%) and non-Turkic (N = 1660; 61.5% [with Persian/Fars, N = 980 subgrouping]) groups, and demographic, clinical manifestations, and immunogenic laboratory findings were extracted from medical records. Mean age at BD onset was 25.72 ± 10.02 years in Turkic patients and 24.69 ± 10.23 years in non-Turkic patients, and males comprised 61.3% and 57.1% of the two groups, respectively. Human leukocyte antigen (HLA)-B5 positivity was 55.1% in Turkic versus 53.1% in non-Turkic patients, and HLA-B51 positivity was 48.7% versus 46.5%, respectively. Most clinical manifestations showed similar prevalence across groups, including oral aphthous ulcers (98.7% vs. 99.0%), genital aphthous ulcers (60.5% vs. 62.0%), uveitis (50.1% vs. 53.2%), and deep vein thrombosis (5.3% vs. 5.1%). Superficial phlebitis was more frequent in Turkic patients (p = 0.02), and oral aphthous ulcers occurred earlier in Turkic patients (p = 0.023). A three-class latent class model demonstrated the best fit (BIC = 14,986.58). In multinomial logistic regression analysis, Turkic patients had slightly higher odds ratio of the ocular-predominant phenotype (OR = 1.10, 95% CI: 0.91-1.33; p = 0.320) and slightly lower odds ratio of the multisystem phenotype (OR = 0.94, 95% CI: 0.68-1.30; p = 0.692); however, neither association was statistically significant. Female gender was associated with higher odds ratio of the ocular-predominant phenotype than the mucocutaneous-predominant phenotype (OR = 1.38, 95% CI: 1.14-1.67; p = 0.001). In this large Iranian BD cohort, Turkic and non-Turkic patients exhibited broadly similar disease phenotypes and comparable HLA-B51 frequencies, with small but potentially relevant ethnic differences in the timing of oral ulcers and the frequency of superficial phlebitis. These findings suggest that ethnicity may influence BD phenotype through mechanisms beyond HLA-B51, possibly involving other immune-related genetic variants such as tumor necrosis factor (TNF)-α, endoplasmic reticulum aminopeptidase 1(ERAP1), Interleukin (IL)-10. Of note, the significant differences observed in Turkic versus non-Turkic comparisons were not present in the Turkic versus Persian (Fars) comparison, indicating that the findings are not driven by a single ethnic subgroup.

items.title: Identification and Validation of Hub Genes Associated With Periodontitis and Systemic Lupus Erythematosus.
items.abstract: Accumulating evidence suggests a close relationship between periodontitis and systemic lupus erythematosus (SLE); however, the shared molecular mechanisms underlying this association remain unclear. This study aimed to identify candidate genes and molecular features shared between periodontitis and SLE through integrative bioinformatics analysis and clinical validation. Gene expression profiles were obtained from the Gene Expression Omnibus (GEO) database, and differentially expressed genes (DEGs) shared between periodontitis and SLE were identified. Gene Ontology (GO) and Kyoto Encyclopedia of Genes and Genomes (KEGG) enrichment analyses were performed, followed by protein-protein interaction (PPI) network construction and hub gene screening. The expression patterns of the hub genes were evaluated in independent validation datasets, and their discriminatory performance was assessed by receiver operating characteristic (ROC) curve analysis. Immune cell infiltration and its correlations with hub gene expression were further investigated. Transcription factor-microRNA regulatory networks and candidate compounds were computationally predicted. Finally, quantitative real-time PCR (qPCR) was performed to validate hub gene expression in clinical samples. A total of 124 overlapping DEGs were identified, from which five hub genes-CCL3, LY96, FOS, MMP9, and PTGS2-were selected. GO and KEGG enrichment analyses indicated that the overlapping DEGs were predominantly associated with inflammatory and immune-related biological processes and signaling pathways. All five hub genes showed consistent expression patterns in the independent periodontitis validation dataset, whereas FOS, LY96, and PTGS2, but not CCL3 and MMP9, showed consistent differential expression in the independent SLE validation dataset. ROC analyses demonstrated varying discriminatory performance across the analyzed datasets. Immune infiltration analysis revealed differences in estimated immune cell profiles in both disease datasets, and computational prediction identified candidate regulatory interactions and compounds for further investigation. qPCR validation in clinical samples (n = 15 per group) showed significantly increased expression of all five hub genes in gingival tissues from patients with periodontitis and PBMCs from patients with SLE compared with their respective healthy controls. This study identified CCL3, LY96, FOS, MMP9, and PTGS2 as candidate genes associated with periodontitis and SLE. FOS, LY96, and PTGS2 showed consistent expression patterns across datasets, whereas CCL3 and MMP9 exhibited dataset-dependent variation in SLE. Clinical qPCR validation showed increased expression of all five genes in both disease cohorts. These findings provide insight into the shared molecular features of periodontitis and SLE and warrant further validation in larger, independent, and clinically well-characterized cohorts.

items.title: Evaluation of factors affecting physical activity and physical function in women with primary sjogren syndrome.
items.abstract: This study aimed to investigate the factors affecting physical activity and physical function in primary Sjogren syndrome. In total, 63 women with primary Sjogren syndrome were examined for physical activity using the International Physical Activity Questionnaire, identified barriers to activity via the Self-Perceived Barriers for Physical Activity Questionnaire, and assessed physical function with the 30-s sit-to-stand and grip strength tests. Disease activity was measured with the EULAR Sjögren's Syndrome Disease Activity Index, symptom severity with the EULAR Sjogren's Syndrome Patient Reported Index, and fatigue using the Multidimensional Fatigue Inventory. Anxiety and depression levels were evaluated with the Hospital Anxiety and Depression Scale, while health perception was assessed with the Health Perception Scale. A one-unit increase in the HPS_Center of control score was associated with a 23.1-point increase in the median International Physical Activity Questionnaire total score (95%CIs 0.55; 63.52). An increase in the Hospital Anxiety and Depression Scale-Anxiety, Hospital Anxiety and Depression Scale-Depression, and MFI_total scores is associated with a rise in the Self-Perceived Barriers for Physical Activity Questionnaire score (0.69 [0.42; 1.13]), (1.07 [0.58; 1.41]), and (0.25 [0.1; 0.3]), respectively. Conversely, grip strength was associated with EULAR Sjogren's Syndrome Patient Reported Index, Hospital Anxiety and Depression Scale-Depression, and MFI_Reduced Motivation (-0.44 [-0.86; -0.01]), (-0.26 [-0.41; -0.08]), and (-0.22 [-0.48; -0.08]), respectively. However, the HPS_Self-awareness score had a positive effect on the 30-s sit-to-stand (0.18 [0.11; 0.3]). In women with primary Sjogren syndrome, emotional symptoms and fatigue were negatively associated with physical activity and function. Better health perception was positively associated with both. Health education and management of emotional disorders and fatigue can improve physical activity and function in primary Sjogren syndrome.

items.title: Psychological Experiences of Adults with Rheumatoid Arthritis: A Systematic Review and Qualitative Evidence Synthesis.
items.abstract: Rheumatoid arthritis (RA) causes unpredictable pain, progressive joint damage, and visible deformities. These features give rise to emotional and relational challenges, including fear of disability, loss of independence, and struggles with identity and social roles. This meta-synthesis aimed to systematically synthesize qualitative evidence on the psychological experiences of patients with RA to inform holistic nursing care. This is a qualitative meta-synthesis. Two reviewers systematically searched six electronic databases (PubMed, Embase, CINAHL, PsycINFO, Web of Science, and Scopus) from inception to March 28, 2026, supplemented by reference list screening. English-language qualitative studies on the psychological experiences of adults with RA were included. Methodological quality was assessed using the Critical Appraisal Skills Program checklist. Reflexive thematic analysis was used for qualitative evidence synthesis. Reporting adhered to the PRISMA and ENTREQ guidelines. The protocol was registered with PROSPERO (CRD420261355146). Thirty-three studies including 663 participants from ten countries were included. Three themes and twelve subthemes were generated: negative emotional experiences (helplessness, fear, guilt, loneliness); self-identity and meaning-making (bodily alienation, role loss, causal attributions, acceptance); and psychological conflicts in interpersonal interactions (dependence vs autonomy, reversed family roles, perceived stigma and pressure to conceal, estrangement in clinical encounters). The psychological burden extends beyond depression and anxiety, involving embodied distress and relational difficulties, yet patients also actively reconstruct meaning. Healthcare professionals can attend to the specific fears, identity struggles, and interpersonal tensions that patients describe. Asking open-ended questions about the most difficult aspects of living with the condition, validating subjective experiences, involving family members in discussions about role adjustments, and reinforcing patients' own adaptive efforts may contribute to more holistic nursing assessment and individualized care.

items.title: Iron Metabolism-associated Biomarkers in Rheumatoid Arthritis: A Meta-analysis of Diagnostic Value and Anemia-related Changes.
items.abstract: Rheumatoid arthritis (RA) is associated with profound alterations in iron metabolism, contributing to chronic inflammation, immune dysfunction, and, in some cases, the development of anemia. This systematic review and meta-analysis evaluated serum biomarkers of iron metabolism in RA patients compared to healthy controls and assessed differences between anemic and non-anemic RA subgroups. PubMed, Embase, Scopus, and Web of Science were systematically searched up to December 2024. Nineteen studies (n = 1,640) were included for the RA versus healthy control analysis, and six studies (n = 325) for the anemia subgroup comparison. Random-effects meta-analyses were performed to calculate standardized mean differences (SMDs) with 95% confidence intervals (CI). Risk of bias was assessed using the Newcastle-Ottawa Scale (NOS), and meta-regression was used to explore sources of heterogeneity. RA patients had significantly elevated ferritin (SMD = 1.14, p < 0.01), IL-6 (SMD = 3.94, p < 0.01), hepcidin, sTFR, and TNF-α levels, and reduced serum iron (SMD = -1.30, p < 0.01) and transferrin saturation. Hepcidin and transferrin levels were not significantly different. In anemic RA patients, lower iron and higher hepcidin and TIBC levels were observed. Meta-regression analyses did not identify significant moderators of heterogeneity. This meta-analysis indicates that RA is linked to inflammation-induced iron dysregulation, characterized by elevated ferritin levels, diminished serum iron, and functional iron deficiency. These modifications occur independently of anemia; however, anemic individuals exhibit additional alterations, such as elevated hepcidin and TIBC levels. Iron metabolism biomarkers may possess diagnostic and therapeutic significance in rheumatoid arthritis, especially for inflammation-mediated pathways. RA is characterized by systemic iron dysregulation, including ferritin upregulation and functional iron deficiency, independent of anemia. These findings highlight potential targets for future therapeutic strategies and improved disease monitoring.

items.title: Early warning and risk assessment of cardiac involvement in dermatomyositis/polymyositis: from biomarkers to multimodal imaging.
items.abstract: Idiopathic inflammatory myopathies (IIM) comprise a broad spectrum of clinical and pathological subtypes, including dermatomyositis (DM), anti-synthetase syndrome, immune-mediated necrotising myopathy (IMNM), overlap myositis, inclusion-body myositis, and polymyositis (PM). Among these, DM remains well-defined, whereas PM has become increasingly rare under current classification criteria. A significant number of early studies categorised patients collectively under the term "DM/PM". Cardiac involvement is recognised as a significant cause of mortality in these patients. The reported incidence of cardiac involvement in DM/PM varies widely and is frequently subclinical. The symptoms are frequently masked by manifestations in the skeletal muscles and the skin, which makes an early diagnosis difficult using conventional examination methods. Although endomyocardial biopsy is regarded as the gold standard, its invasive nature limits its clinical application. It is therefore imperative to establish an efficient framework for early warning and precise risk assessment of cardiac involvement in DM/PM. In this review, we summarize current and emerging evidence on serum biomarkers and multimodal imaging for the early identification and risk assessment of cardiac involvement in DM/PM. These advances are built on the evolving classification system for IIM.The integration of these tools with clinical high-risk factors is intended to facilitate the construction of a comprehensive risk assessment model. This integrated approach is intended to facilitate the early detection and treatment of cardiac involvement in DM/PM patients, thereby improving their prognosis.

items.title: Development of an IL-6- and Th1/Treg-based nomogram for identifying low bone mass in patients with rheumatoid arthritis.
items.abstract: This study aimed to analyze clinical and immunological characteristics in patients with rheumatoid arthritis (RA) according to bone loss status, integrate traditional risk factors with immune-inflammatory indicators, and construct and validate an individualized nomogram for estimating the probability of concurrent BMD-defined low bone mass in patients with RA. A total of 442 patients with RA were enrolled and divided into normal bone mass (RA-N, n=219) and low bone mass (RA-LBM, n=223) groups based on bone mineral density values. Data on the clinical characteristics, laboratory parameters, peripheral blood lymphocyte subsets, and cytokine levels were collected for both groups. The Benjamini-Hochberg (BH) method was applied for multiple testing correction. Univariate logistic regression was used to screen relevant variables, and the random forest algorithm (mean decrease Gini importance ranking and out-of-bag error analysis) was employed to determine the optimal combination of variables. Multivariate logistic regression was performed to identify factors independently associated with low bone mass, based on which a nomogram for identifying concurrent low bone mass was constructed. The discriminative ability of the model was evaluated using the receiver operating characteristic curve, calibration was assessed using the calibration curve and Hosmer-Lemeshow test, and clinical net benefit was evaluated using decision curve analysis. Patients in the RA-LBM group exhibited significantly higher values for age, disease duration, erythrocyte sedimentation rate, aspartate aminotransferase/alanine aminotransferase ratio, and alkaline phosphatase, while body mass index (BMI), red blood cell count, hemoglobin levels, albumin levels, and albumin/globulin ratio were significantly lower than those in the RA-N group (BH-adjusted P<0.05). Immunological analysis revealed that interleukin-6 (IL-6) levels were significantly elevated in the RA-LBM group (BH-adjusted P<0.001), and the T helper 1 cell/regulatory T cell (Th1/Treg) ratio was also significantly increased (BH-adjusted P = 0.016). Random forest analysis followed by multivariate logistic regression ultimately identified age, Th1/Treg ratio, BMI, IL-6, albumin, and uric acid levels as factors independently associated with low bone mass in patients with RA (BH-adjusted P<0.05). Model 1 constructed based on these six variables achieved an area under the curve (AUC) of 0.906 (95% CI: 0.877-0.935), which was significantly higher than that of model 2 containing only traditional risk factors (AUC = 0.861, P = 0.001). The AUCs of model 1 in the training and validation sets were 0.906 and 0.905, respectively. The Hosmer-Lemeshow test indicated good model calibration. Decision curve analysis showed that the model provided a higher net benefit than the treat-all and treat-none strategies across a range of threshold probabilities. This study integrates immune-inflammatory indicators, such as IL-6 and Th1/Treg ratio, with traditional risk factors to construct a nomogram for identifying concurrent BMD-defined low bone mass in patients with RA. The model showed favorable discrimination and calibration and may provide a useful tool for estimating the probability of concurrent low bone mass in this population.

items.title: Case Report: Sacrococcygeal teratoma with malignant transformation into mixed adenocarcinoma and squamous cell carcinoma following TNF-α inhibitor therapy for ankylosing spondylitis.
items.abstract: Adult sacrococcygeal teratoma (SCT) with malignant transformation is exceptionally rare, and its occurrence during long-term tumor necrosis factor-α (TNF-α) inhibitor therapy has never been reported. This case firstly links prolonged TNF-α blockade-used for ankylosing spondylitis-with aggressive biphenotypic (i.e. adenocarcinoma and squamous cell carcinoma (SCC)) transformation of congenital SCT. Serial biopsies over time enabled dynamic tracking of histological changes from adenocarcinoma toward SCC, a phenomenon not previously documented in malignant SCT. The concurrent TP53 and KRAS G12D mutations further distinguish this case and suggest a potential targeted therapeutic avenue. A 31-year-old woman with two prior resections of gluteal masses and six-year TNF-α inhibitor exposure presented with a recurrent gluteal mass. Imaging revealed a pelvic-sacral mass and a gluteal subcutaneous soft tissue mass. Biopsy of the pelvic tumour only described intestinal-type adenocarcinoma; however, subsequent gluteal biopsy disclosed mixed components of 65% SCC and 35% adenocarcinoma. The origin diagnosis was malignant SCT with adeno-squamous transformation, IV stage with pelvic and gluteal metastases. Unfortunately, the patient successively developed local recurrence at the sacrococcygeal region and widespread metastases involving liver, inguinal lymph nodes, bone, lungs, and kidneys, although multidisciplinary Interventions were administered including resection, chemotherapy and radiotherapy. Clinicians should learn two key lessons from this case. First, it is imperative to sustain vigilance for malignant transformation in patients with a history of recurrent SCT, and regular follow-up is strongly advised. Second, although current meta-analyses demonstrate no statistically significant association between TNF-α inhibitor exposure and overall malignancy risk, the physiological role of TNF-α in immune surveillance, together with relevant clinical guidelines, supports discontinuation of these agents upon diagnosis of a solid malignancy. In this case, given the aggressive tumor behavior and the availability of alternative agents for ankylosing spondylitis, we elected to pause TNF-α blockade as a precautionary, guideline-informed clinical judgment.

items.title: Associations between thyrotropin receptor antibody, rheumatoid autoantibodies, and disease activity in patients with rheumatoid arthritis: a retrospective cross-sectional study.
items.abstract: Thyrotropin receptor antibody (TRAb) frequently coexists with rheumatoid factor (RF) and anti-cyclic citrullinated peptide antibody (anti-CCP) in patients with rheumatoid arthritis (RA), but its association with disease activity remains unclear. This study assessed the associations of TRAb and rheumatoid autoantibodies with DAS28-ESR in RA patients. This retrospective cross-sectional study enrolled 192 RA patients hospitalized at the First Affiliated Hospital of Guizhou University of Traditional Chinese Medicine between October 2024 and October 2025, all meeting the 2010 ACR/EULAR criteria. Patients were classified as TRAb-positive or TRAb-negative using the clinical cutoff of 1.75 IU/L. Associations between TRAb and DAS28-ESR were evaluated by Spearman correlation, restricted cubic spline (RCS) analysis, and multivariable linear regression. The primary analysis was repeated in euthyroid patients ( n  = 167). Interactions of TRAb with Ln(RF) and Ln(anti-CCP) were tested in all 192 patients, and an exploratory four-group comparison was performed in 138 patients with concordant antibody titers. TRAb correlated positively with DAS28-ESR ( ρ =0.36, P  < 0.001), and RCS analysis revealed a nonlinear association ( P  = 0.002 for nonlinear). hs-CRP, ESR, and DAS28-ESR were higher in TRAb-positive ( n  = 51) than TRAb-negative patients ( n  = 141; all P  < 0.001). After covariate adjustment, TRAb positivity remained independently associated with higher DAS28-ESR ( B  = 1.457, P  < 0.001), and the association persisted in euthyroid patients (4.9 vs. 4.1, P  < 0.001). TRAb showed a statistically significant interaction with Ln(anti-CCP) ( P  = 0.0014) and a borderline interaction with Ln(RF) ( P  = 0.046); DAS28-ESR was highest in TRAb-positive patients with high-titer autoantibodies. TRAb positivity was associated with higher disease activity and systemic inflammation in RA patients, including those with normal thyroid function, and the association strengthened with increasing rheumatoid autoantibody titers. The value of combined TRAb, RF, and anti-CCP testing for immune stratification in RA warrants prospective validation.

items.title: Metachronous sequential involvement of rice-body bursitis in the shoulder and knee: a case report of rare polyarticular presentation in a patient with rheumatoid arthritis.
items.abstract: Rice-body bursitis is an uncommon complication of rheumatoid arthritis (RA). Metachronous involvement of multiple joints has rarely been described. We report a 52-year-old woman with a 16-year history of RA who presented in 2019 with refractory swelling of the right shoulder. Ultrasound and MRI revealed "honeycomb-like" effusion and T2-hypointense particles within the subacromial-subdeltoid bursa, leading to a probable imaging-based diagnosis of rice-body bursitis. She achieved complete remission approximately 6 months after adalimumab was started, during which leflunomide was continued; adalimumab was then discontinued by the patient. In April 2026, left knee swelling recurred, ESR was 37 mm/h and CRP was 1.842 mg/dl, while other joint symptoms were minimal. MRI showed numerous floating particles and T2-low-signal bodies, and arthroscopic exploration confirmed rice-body bursitis of the knee. After arthroscopic debridement, the knee symptoms resolved completely within one week. The two episodes occurred 7 years apart and involved different joints, indicating that rice-body bursitis in RA can present as a metachronous sequential condition. Inflammatory marker levels did not parallel the severity of local joint involvement in this patient. This case underscores that rice-body bursitis should be considered in RA patients with refractory monoarthritis. Arthroscopic clearance combined with systemic antirheumatic therapy was followed by resolution of knee symptoms within one week in this patient. Because the two episodes involved different joints, disease phases, and concurrent treatments, no comparison between treatment strategies can be made.

items.title: Granulomatosis with polyangiitis masquerading as lung cancer with meningeal metastasis: a case report and literature review.
items.abstract: Granulomatosis with polyangiitis (GPA) is an anti-neutrophil cytoplasmic antibody (ANCA)-associated small-vessel vasculitis classically presenting with upper and lower respiratory tract and renal involvement. Central nervous system (CNS) involvement in GPA is rare and is highly prone to being misdiagnosed as intracranial tumor metastasis or intracranial infection. We report a 60-year-old female who presented with recurrent headache and conjunctival injection. She had undergone two surgical procedures for "glaucoma" at an outside hospital without headache relief. Upon admission to our hospital, chest CT revealed multiple bilateral pulmonary nodules, highly suspicious for lung cancer; brain MRI showed dural thickening with subdural effusion; lumbar puncture revealed an intracranial pressure (ICP) of 270 mmH₂O, with negative CSF cultures and no tumor cells. The initial diagnosis was leptomeningeal metastasis from lung cancer. However, percutaneous lung biopsy showed no evidence of tumor or infection, and serology revealed positive c-ANCA/PR3-ANCA, leading to a final diagnosis of GPA with clinicoradiologically supported GPA-related pachymeningitis. After glucocorticoid therapy, the patient's headache and other symptoms resolved rapidly. We reviewed 33 published cases of GPA with cranial involvement and summarized their clinical features. Hypertrophic pachymeningitis (HP) was the most common cranial manifestation (51.5%). Serum ANCA positivity was 87.9% (29/33). Among all 33 cases, c-ANCA/PR3-ANCA was reported in 23 (69.7%); among the 29 ANCA-positive cases, c-ANCA/PR3-ANCA accounted for 79.3% (23/29). After immunosuppressive or immunomodulatory therapy, approximately 90.9% of patients improved or stabilized. These features may serve as clues that should prompt clinicians to consider GPA in the differential diagnosis of pulmonary nodules with pachymeningeal disease and raised intracranial pressure, rather than as established discriminators from lung cancer brain metastasis. GPA can present with multiple pulmonary masses, headache, and pachymeningitis, closely mimicking leptomeningeal metastasis of lung cancer. When imaging and clinical presentation are atypical, serum ANCA testing and pathological biopsy are key to differential diagnosis. Clinicians should be alert to this "mimic of malignancy" to avoid unnecessary surgery or radiotherapy.
